headline: Migration-focused trips need more time than standard safaris
summary: A standard Tanzania safari can work in 5-7 days. Migration-focused trips benefit from 8-12 days to account for positioning, transit between regions, and waiting for unpredictable events. For river crossings specifically, 4-5 nights in the crossing zone provides approximately 70% probability of witnessing at least one crossing. Shorter trips should set realistic expectations or focus on calving.

assumptions.text: Crossing probability increases significantly with nights spent in crossing zone.
Migration positioning often requires transit between regions.
Migration focus typically requires 2-4 more days than standard safari.

gains: 8-12 days: Allows proper positioning and waiting time
4-5 nights in crossing zone: ~70% crossing probability
Extra days: Flexibility to follow herd movements
Combined itinerary: Migration plus reliable areas
losses: Short trip focused on migration: High disappointment risk
More time does not guarantee specific events

change_conditions: If trip is under 7 days, focus on calving or accept migration as bonus.
If crossings are priority, minimum 4-5 nights in crossing zone.
If flexible on time, 10-12 days provides best migration experience.
If budget limits length, prioritize nights in key zone over breadth.
